chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Ali ibn Abu Abdullah, from Al-Husayn ibn Yazeed, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying, and Abu Haneefah had said to him, 'The people were astonished at you yesterday while you were at Arafat, haggling over your sacrificial camels with the most intense bargaining.' He said, so Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'And what is the Pleasure of Allah if I am cheated in my wealth?' He said, so Abu Haneefah said, 'No, by Allah! There is little or much Pleasure of Allah in this, and we do not come to you with anything except that you come to us with what there is no way out for us from.'

key_terms.عَرَفَةَ: Arafat, the plain near Mecca where the standing (wuquf) of Hajj takes place
key_terms.لَا مَخْرَجَ لَنَا مِنْهُ: There is no way out for us from it

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Sadiq haggle over the price of sacrificial animals at Arafat?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the practical wisdom of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in economic transactions, illustrating his mastery of market dynamics during Hajj. Abu Haneefah’s admission that the Imam’s arguments were 'inescapable' underscores the depth of Shia jurisprudential reasoning in daily life. The narrative serves as a critique of rigid scholarly pride, emphasizing that maximizing one's wealth is not merely a worldly concern but aligns with divine pleasure when done justly.
